findings.issue: For greater precision, label the first and third rows explicitly as enthalpic contributions—for example, “positive ΔH contribution, tending to raise ΔG°” and “negative ΔH contribution, tending to lower ΔG°.”
findings.evidence: As standard chemistry, energy cost or release establishes an enthalpy contribution, while ΔG° also includes the −TΔS° term. The source likewise gives every factor both enthalpic and entropic contributions. The table’s hedged “Typical” wording and the balanced Full-credit answer prevent an outright contradiction, but the clearer labels would avoid reading energy cost or release as sufficient by itself to determine ΔG°.
